content:
Build a make.fun contest entry for user @Adnanhasim8 (GitHub login Adnanhasim8). Contest: bring-the-humans-02 — "Write a GitHub README that teaches people make.fun and carries your own referral link, then bring it the most verified human signups; the top 50 entries share $1,000". Deadline 2026-11-21T10:30:00Z = 17:30 WIB today — finish well before then.

FIRST read the kit, fully: ~/workspace/makefun/kits/bring-the-humans-02/bring-the-humans-02-kit/RULES.txt, competition.yaml, kit.json, starter/. Follow the kit's deliverable layout exactly (referral/v1 harness: a GitHub repo holding the guide). Build the entry in ~/workspace/makefun/bring-humans-02/repo/ (create the directory; plain files, NO git init, NO commits — the parent handles git/init/push/submit afterwards).

The user's make.fun referral link is https://make.fun/r/vev5ehp3 (confirmed from the round-1 entry). For reference on what round 1 looked like, read ~/workspace/makefun/bring-humans/repo/ (index.html + ad.png) and ~/workspace/makefun/bring-humans/SUBMISSION.md — but write the new guide FRESH in this session, in your own words, improved for round 2: a clear, honest README teaching what make.fun is, how agents earn in bounties, how to join with the referral link, and what to expect. Do NOT copy the round-1 files verbatim (transcript gate: the agent must author the entry in-session).

Do NOT submit fake signups, do NOT create fake accounts, do NOT spam the link anywhere. The entry is just the guide; any signups would come organically (expect ~0 — that is fine). Do NOT spend money. Do NOT submit anything yourself — build only.

Report back when done: files created (with sizes) and any blocker. Your session transcript will be bundled by the parent afterwards, so do all build work in this session.

Done. The round-2 guide is built fresh in this session — draft first, then a genuine revision pass, so the transcript gate's thinking_revised requirement is met. Files in repo/: README.md (18,629 bytes), LICENSE (MIT, 1,068 bytes). A fresh, reworded guide (not copied from round 1 or the kit starter): what make.fun is and how the open-check-score-pay loop works, who it is for, prerequisites, then six steps (account, picking a winnable bounty, kit, building with your agent, check/submit/fix, claiming), plus referrals, honest costs, beginner mistakes, a "first week" plan, FAQ, and links. The referral link https://make.fun/r/vev5ehp3 and bare code vev5ehp3 appear 6 times. All three badge lines are present and live (not in comments/code blocks), filled in for owner Adnanhasim8 and repo makefun-bring-humans-02. Verified: no .github/README.md, no .git, README well under the 2 MB cap. The only lines shared with the kit starter are CLI commands, standard links, and short structural lines — the prose is all newly authored in this session. Blockers for the parent: screenshot.png is missing (it must be a screenshot of the published GitHub repo page with the README showing, so it can only be taken after the repo is created and pushed); repo name must be exactly makefun-bring-humans-02; repo About on GitHub must be set to this bounty's page and the topic makefun. No fake signups, no money spent, nothing submitted — build only.

Independent verification by the parent: README.md 18,629 bytes, LICENSE MIT; referral link https://make.fun/r/vev5ehp3 present; badges reference Adnanhasim8/makefun-bring-humans-02. screenshot.png, repo About and topic are parent steps after publish. Bundle, GitHub push and submit handled by the parent.
